items.stem: Which observation is the strongest sign that a chemical reaction has occurred?

options.text: A new substance with different properties has formed
options.rationale: Correct: forming a new substance is the key sign of a chemical reaction.
Changing shape is a physical change, not a reaction.

options.text: The material got colder in the fridge
options.rationale: Cooling alone is usually a physical change.

options.text: The material was poured into a new cup
options.rationale: Pouring changes location, not the substance.

items.explanation: Correct: forming a new substance is the key sign of a chemical reaction.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are examples of chemical reactions? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

options.text: Wood burning into ash and smoke
options.rationale: Correct: burning forms new substances and is a chemical reaction.
Melting is a physical change; it is still water.
Dissolving is a physical change; the sugar is unchanged.

items.explanation: Correct: rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

items.stem: In the reaction 'iron + oxygen -> rust', which is the product?

options.rationale: Correct: rust is the new substance formed, so it is the product.
Iron is a reactant, a starting material.
Oxygen is a reactant, a starting material.
Temperature is not a substance in the equation.

items.explanation: Correct: rust is the new substance formed, so it is the product.
